bibliographic.abstract: During the past decade, CoFe2O4 (hard)/Co−Fe alloy (soft) magnetic nanocomposites have been routinely prepared by partial reduction of CoFe2O4 nanoparticles. Monoxide (i.e., FeO or CoO) has often been detected as a byproduct of the reduction, although it remains unclear whether the formation of this phase occurs during the reduction itself or at a later stage. Here, a novel reaction cell was designed to monitor the reduction in situ using synchrotron powder X-ray diffraction (PXRD). Sequential Rietveld refinements of the in situ data yielded time-resolved information on the sample composition and confirmed that the monoxide is generated as an intermediate phase. The macroscopic magnetic properties of samples at different reduction stages were measured by means of vibrating sample magnetometry (VSM), revealing a magnetic softening with increasing soft phase content, which was too pronounced to be exclusively explained by the introduction of soft material in the system. The elemental compositions of the constituent phases were obtained from joint Rietveld refinements of ex situ high-resolution PXRD and neutron powder diffraction (NPD) data. It was found that the alloy has a tendency to emerge in a Co-rich form, inducing a Co deficiency on the remaining spinel phase, which can explain the early softening of the magnetic material.

datasets.dataset_description: PXRD data with a time resolution of 5 s were measured up to 2θ = 18° in reduction experiments using synchrotron radiation with a wavelength of 0.207 00 Å and a beam size of 0.5 × 0.5 mm2 at beamline P02.1; gas flow (5, 10, 20, and 30mL/min at 400 °C) and the temperature (300, 350, 400, and 500 °C at 10 mL/min).

PXRD data were collected with a Rigaku SmartLab diffractometer in Bragg-Brentano θ/θ geometry with a diffracted beam monochromator in front of a D/teX Ultra detector using X-rays generated by Cu Kα and Co Kα anodes.

NPD data were collected for all the samples at DMC using a wavelength of 2.458 97(11) Å and in the q-range 0.5−3.7 Å−1 and additionally collected for the partially reduced composites at HRPT using a wavelength of 1.493 65(7) Å and in the q-range 0.3−8.3 Å−1.
Field-dependent magnetization curves were measured at 300 K as a function of an externally applied field along the direction normal to the pellet surface and in the range ±2T.
